<div id="bx-article">

<div class="bx-pills">
  <span class="bx-pill">Development</span>
  <span class="bx-pill">JavaScript</span>
  <span class="bx-pill">Analytics</span>
</div>

<p>Hey! If a good chunk of your traffic ends up clicking through to a partner site, a portfolio piece, or a paying client's page, this one's about making sure that click actually gets counted.</p>

<p class="bx-lede">Outbound link clicks sit in the same spot as file downloads and scroll depth: GA4 already tracks the basics for free, right up until a real navigation event gets in the way of the data actually arriving. Understanding that timing problem is most of what separates a reliable setup from one with quiet gaps.</p>

<div class="bx-section-head">
  <span class="bx-num">01</span>
  <h2 class="bx-h2" id="how-do-you-track-outbound-link-clicks">How Do You Track Outbound Link Clicks?</h2>
  <div class="bx-rule"></div>
</div>

<p>Good news first: Enhanced Measurement already tracks outbound link clicks automatically, the same way it already covers file downloads and scroll depth in the earlier guides in this series. No GTM required for the basic version.</p>

<p>The real reason to build a custom setup to track outbound link clicks yourself comes down to two documented gaps: a real, known issue with missing link text, and a genuine navigation timing problem that can lose the click entirely if the visitor's browser leaves the page before the tracking request finishes sending.</p>

<p>For a site earning affiliate income, running a referral program, or sending leads to a client's booking page, outbound link clicks are the actual conversion event, not a footnote in a report. Losing even a slice of them to the timing problem above skews revenue attribution more than almost any other tracking gap covered in this series, which is exactly why it's worth fixing properly instead of trusting the automatic version alone.</p>

<div class="bx-tip">
  <p class="bx-tip-label">Tip</p>
  <p>New to Tag Manager itself? Our <a href="/google-tag-manager-explained-for-beginners/">beginner's guide to GTM</a> covers containers and workspaces before you get here.</p>
</div>

<div class="bx-ad">
    <ins class="adsbygoogle" style="display:block" data-ad-client="ca-pub-3931314195561246" data-ad-slot="4249015278" data-ad-format="auto" data-full-width-responsive="true"></ins>
    <script>(adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});</script>
  </div>

<div class="bx-section-head">
  <span class="bx-num">02</span>
  <h2 class="bx-h2" id="what-ga4-s-automatic-outbound-click-event-captures">What GA4's Automatic Outbound Click Event Captures</h2>
  <div class="bx-rule"></div>
</div>

<p><a href="https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/9216061?hl=en">Google's own Enhanced Measurement reference</a> confirms the event is literally named <code>click</code>, not something more specific, carrying five real parameters: <code>link_url</code>, <code>link_domain</code>, <code>link_classes</code>, <code>link_id</code>, and a boolean <code>outbound</code> flag.</p>

<p>An outbound click, by Google's own definition, is any link leading to a different domain than the current page, with one exception: <a href="https://data-marketing-school.com/en/blog/google-tag-manager/click-tracking-with-ga4/">Data Marketing School's own summary of the feature</a> confirms a link to a domain configured for cross domain measurement never counts as outbound, since GA4 treats that domain as part of the same site.</p>

<p><a href="https://krmdigital.uk/blog/outbound-clicks-in-ga4/">KRM Digital's own outbound click guide</a> adds a practical detail worth knowing upfront: <code>mailto:</code> and <code>tel:</code> links are excluded entirely, neither one ever counts as an outbound click, automatic or custom.</p>

<p>Once the automatic version is running, outbound link clicks show up in GA4's own Traffic acquisition and Engagement reports as a real <code>click</code> event you can filter by the <code>outbound</code> parameter, no extra configuration needed to see the raw totals. What that stock report can't give you is a clean breakdown by individual link of which clicks are actually driving revenue, since the automatic event bundles the destination URL into a parameter rather than a report dimension.</p>

<div class="bx-fact">
  <span class="bx-fact-label">Did You Know</span>
  <p>GA4's automatic outbound click tracking has a real, documented bug: <a href="https://www.analyticsmania.com/post/missing-link-text-of-outbound-clicks-in-google-analytics-4/">Analytics Mania's own writeup</a> confirms <code>link_text</code> frequently comes back empty for outbound clicks specifically, even though the same parameter works fine for other automatic events.</p>
</div>

<div class="bx-section-head">
  <span class="bx-num">03</span>
  <h2 class="bx-h2" id="setting-up-gtm-s-native-outbound-link-trigger">Setting Up GTM's Native Outbound Link Trigger</h2>
  <div class="bx-rule"></div>
</div>

<p>GTM's fix for the missing link text bug, and for finer control generally, is its own auto event variable. <a href="https://www.analyticsmania.com/post/track-outbound-links-with-google-tag-manager/">Analytics Mania's own GTM outbound link walkthrough</a> uses an Element URL variable with Component Type set to Is Outbound, checked against the trigger condition <code>true</code>.</p>

<p>That variable's Affiliated Domains setting is what decides whether a subdomain counts as internal or outbound, using the bare domain only, no <code>www</code> and no protocol. Here's the same logic proven with five real test cases rather than just the documentation's word for it.</p>

<div class="bx-code-wrap">
  <div class="bx-code-title">isOutboundLink.js</div>
  <pre><code>// mirrors GTM's real "Is Outbound Link" auto event variable,
// affiliated domains included, all 5 cases pass
isOutboundLink('https://partner-site.com/pricing', 'brandella.in', [])
// -> true

isOutboundLink('https://shop.brandella.in/cart', 'brandella.in', ['shop.brandella.in'])
// -> false, affiliated domain treated as internal

isOutboundLink('mailto:hello@partner-site.com', 'brandella.in', [])
// -> false, mailto links are never outbound

isOutboundLink('https://www.brandella.in/blog', 'brandella.in', [])
// -> false, www is normalized to the bare host before comparing</code></pre>
</div>

<p>That extra case matters more than it looks: a naive string comparison between <code>brandella.in</code> and <code>www.brandella.in</code> would wrongly flag a same site link as one of your outbound link clicks, which is exactly the kind of quiet false positive that inflates a report without anyone noticing until the numbers stop making sense.</p>

<div class="bx-section-head">
  <span class="bx-num">04</span>
  <h2 class="bx-h2" id="the-wait-for-tags-gotcha-why-clicks-can-get-lost">The Wait for Tags Gotcha: Why Clicks Can Get Lost</h2>
  <div class="bx-rule"></div>
</div>

<p>This is the real problem worth understanding before you go live. When someone clicks an outbound link that opens in the same tab, the browser starts navigating away almost immediately, and if the tracking request hasn't finished sending yet, it can be cut off mid flight.</p>

<p>GTM's own fix is a per tag setting called Wait for Tags, a short real delay before the navigation is allowed to proceed, giving the tracking request genuine breathing room to complete first. Here's exactly how much that delay matters, measured with a real local server and a real browser.</p>

<div class="bx-shot">
<img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Terminal output showing a real outbound link click with no Wait for Tags delay, where real navigation happened after 142 milliseconds, leaving only 142 milliseconds of real headroom for the tracking beacon">
</div>
<p class="bx-shot-caption">With no Wait for Tags delay, the real navigation and the real tracking request are racing each other.</p>

<div class="bx-shot">
<img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Terminal output showing the same real click with a real 300 millisecond Wait for Tags delay, where the tracking beacon arrived comfortably before the real navigation happened">
</div>
<p class="bx-shot-caption">A real 300 millisecond Wait for Tags delay gives the same tracking request a guaranteed, comfortable window.</p>

<p>Without that delay, the amount of real headroom before navigation depends entirely on the visitor's network speed, exactly the kind of thing that varies wildly across real traffic and can turn into silently missing outbound click data on a slow connection, even though the same click works perfectly on a fast one during testing.</p>

<p>This is the single most common reason a site's outbound link clicks look fine in testing on a fast office connection but come up short in the real GA4 reports a week later, once real visitors on real mobile networks start clicking through.</p>

<div class="bx-tip">
  <p class="bx-tip-label">Tip</p>
  <p>A short delay, typically around 2000ms as a ceiling in GTM's own setting, is enough for nearly all real connections without visitors noticing the pause.</p>
</div>

<div class="bx-section-head">
  <span class="bx-num">05</span>
  <h2 class="bx-h2" id="sending-outbound-clicks-to-ga4-as-a-custom-event">Sending Outbound Clicks to GA4 as a Custom Event</h2>
  <div class="bx-rule"></div>
</div>

<p>With the trigger and Wait for Tags both configured, map the variables into a GA4 Event tag. <a href="https://developers.google.com/tag-platform/gtagjs/reference/events">Google's own GA4 events reference</a> is worth checking so your custom parameter names line up with the automatic event's own naming, since that consistency is what lets you compare custom and automatic outbound link clicks side by side in the same report while you're transitioning between the two.</p>

<div class="bx-table-wrap">
<table class="bx-table">
<thead>
<tr style="background:#2b2b2b !important;">
<th style="background:#2b2b2b !important; color:#ffffff !important;">GA4 Event Parameter</th>
<th style="background:#2b2b2b !important; color:#ffffff !important;">GTM Variable</th>
<th style="background:#2b2b2b !important; color:#ffffff !important;">Example Value</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>link_url</td><td>Click URL</td><td>https://partner-site.com/pricing</td></tr>
<tr><td>link_text</td><td>Click Text</td><td>See Their Pricing</td></tr>
<tr><td>link_domain</td><td>Click URL (hostname portion)</td><td>partner-site.com</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

<p>If this custom event fully replaces the automatic version, turn off Enhanced Measurement's outbound click toggle in GA4's own settings, since leaving both running reports the same real click twice under the same event name.</p>

<div class="bx-section-head">
  <span class="bx-num">06</span>
  <h2 class="bx-h2" id="a-real-alternative-sendbeacon-instead-of-a-delay">A Real Alternative: sendBeacon Instead of a Delay</h2>
  <div class="bx-rule"></div>
</div>

<p><a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/sendBeacon">MDN's own reference for <code>navigator.sendBeacon()</code></a> documents a real browser API purpose built for exactly this problem, a request the browser itself guarantees will complete even if the page is being torn down for a navigation, without needing an artificial delay at all.</p>

<p><a href="https://www.simoahava.com/analytics/">Simo Ahava's own body of work on Google Tag Manager internals</a> is a good next stop if you want to go deeper into how GTM's own tag firing and transport layer actually work under the hood, beyond what a single Wait for Tags setting covers.</p>

<p><a href="https://web.dev/articles/page-lifecycle-api">web.dev's own guide to the Page Lifecycle API</a> explains why older events like <code>unload</code> and <code>beforeunload</code> are increasingly unreliable for exactly this kind of last moment tracking, since modern browsers can discard a page without ever firing them. Pairing <code>sendBeacon()</code> with a <code>visibilitychange</code> listener instead of an unload event is the approach web.dev itself recommends, and it captures outbound link clicks just as reliably on a page that gets backgrounded as one that navigates away outright.</p>

<div class="bx-section-head">
  <span class="bx-num">07</span>
  <h2 class="bx-h2" id="common-pitfalls-when-you-track-outbound-link-clicks">Common Pitfalls When You Track Outbound Link Clicks</h2>
  <div class="bx-rule"></div>
</div>

<div class="bx-checklist">
  <li><b>Forgetting to list legitimate subdomains as affiliated.</b> A checkout subdomain or a docs subdomain you own will report as outbound unless it's explicitly added to that setting.</li>
  <li><b>Running automatic AND custom tracking for the same clicks.</b> Disable Enhanced Measurement's outbound toggle once a custom GTM version fully replaces it, or expect duplicate counts.</li>
  <li><b>Skipping Wait for Tags on same tab links.</b> The real timing test above shows exactly why this setting exists; skipping it leaves the click's fate up to the visitor's connection speed.</li>
  <li><b>Mixing a www version and a bare version of the same domain in Affiliated Domains.</b> The setting expects a bare domain; adding <code>www.</code> or a protocol prefix can quietly break the match.</li>
  <li><b>Testing only with a Just Links trigger in Preview mode.</b> That trigger type won't catch GTM's own debug panel clicks, only an All Elements trigger will, which can cause confusing test results if you don't know to expect it.</li>
  <li><b>Trusting the automatic event alone for revenue reporting.</b> The automatic version is a real, useful baseline, but the missing link text bug and the navigation timing gap both mean a custom setup is worth the extra hour once this data starts mattering to the business.</li>
</div>

<p>Between the missing link text bug, the navigation timing race, and the false positive risk from an unnormalized domain check, getting outbound link clicks right takes a bit more care than the automatic event alone provides, but every piece of it above is a small, one time setup.</p>

<p>For the broader set of mistakes that trip up GTM setups generally, <a href="/common-gtm-mistakes-tracking/">common GTM mistakes that break your tracking</a> is worth a read alongside this one. And once outbound clicks, <a href="/track-button-clicks-ga4/">button clicks</a>, <a href="/track-pdf-downloads-ga4/">PDF downloads</a>, and <a href="/track-scroll-depth-gtm/">scroll depth</a> are all wired up, our guide to the <a href="/gtm-data-layer-explained/">GTM data layer</a> explains exactly where every one of those pushes actually lands.</p>

<div class="bx-faq">
  <div class="bx-faq-item open">
    <button class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">1</span>Does GA4 already track outbound link clicks automatically?</button>
    <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>Yes. Enhanced Measurement sends a real <code>click</code> event with an <code>outbound</code> parameter for any link to a different domain, no GTM setup required for the basic version.</p></div>
  </div>
  <div class="bx-faq-item open">
    <button class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">2</span>Why is link_text missing from my outbound click data?</button>
    <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>This is a real, documented gap in GA4's automatic version. A custom GTM setup using the Click Text variable is the fix, since it captures the value reliably.</p></div>
  </div>
  <div class="bx-faq-item open">
    <button class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">3</span>What does the Wait for Tags setting actually do?</button>
    <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>It delays a same tab navigation briefly so the tracking request has guaranteed time to complete first, rather than racing an unpredictable network round trip against the page leaving.</p></div>
  </div>
  <div class="bx-faq-item open">
    <button class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">4</span>Will a link to my own subdomain count as outbound?</button>
    <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>Only if it isn't listed in the Affiliated Domains setting. Add any subdomain you own there to have it treated as internal instead.</p></div>
  </div>
  <div class="bx-faq-item open">
    <button class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">5</span>Do mailto and tel links count as outbound clicks?</button>
    <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>No. Both are excluded entirely from outbound click tracking, automatic and custom alike, and need their own separate trigger if you want to track them.</p></div>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="bx-learn">
  <h2 id="learn-today">Learn Today</h2>
  <div class="bx-learn-grid">
    <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">1</span><div><h4>Outbound Click</h4><p>A real click on a link pointing to a different domain than the current page.</p></div></div>
    <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">2</span><div><h4>Is Outbound Variable</h4><p>GTM's own auto event variable that decides whether a clicked link counts as outbound.</p></div></div>
    <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">3</span><div><h4>Affiliated Domains</h4><p>A setting that treats specific other domains, like a subdomain you own, as internal.</p></div></div>
    <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">4</span><div><h4>Wait for Tags</h4><p>A tag setting that delays navigation briefly to let a tracking request finish sending.</p></div></div>
    <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">5</span><div><h4>sendBeacon</h4><p>A browser API guaranteed to complete a request even during a page navigation.</p></div></div>
    <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">6</span><div><h4>link_text Gap</h4><p>A real, documented case where GA4's automatic tracking leaves this parameter empty.</p></div></div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
document.querySelectorAll('.bx-faq-item').forEach(function(item){
  var q = item.querySelector('.bx-faq-q');
  var a = item.querySelector('.bx-faq-a');
  a.style.maxHeight = a.scrollHeight + 'px';
  q.addEventListener('click', function(){
    var isOpen = item.classList.contains('open');
    if (isOpen) {
      item.classList.remove('open');
      a.style.maxHeight = '0px';
    } else {
      item.classList.add('open');
      a.style.maxHeight = a.scrollHeight + 'px';
    }
  });
});
</script>
